cleanIntro: The CDS9 strips through the slide-stop notch like a 1911 but has two recoil springs on one guide rod and a barrel CAM instead of a link. ⛔ And it has a trap the 1911 does not: with the slide off, engaging the thumb safety can launch the detent plunger out of the frame.

steps.title: Unloaded, inspected, eyes protected
steps.action: Muzzle safe, fingers outside the guard, unload it and LOOK into the magazine well and chamber. Eye protection on before anything moves — the recoil spring is under tension and this pistol has two of them.
steps.quote: Exercise great caution as the recoil spring is under tension and can fly out with enough force to cause serious injury, property damage or loss.
steps.cite: Kimber CDS9 Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Reassembly

steps.title: Cock the hammer, then line the tab up with the notch
steps.action: Cock the hammer first, then move the slide rearward until the semi-circular tab on the back of the slide stop aligns with the semi-circular disassembly notch in the bottom of the slide.
steps.quote: Cock the hammer and move the slide toward the rear until the semi-circular tab on the back of the slide stop aligns with the semi-circular disassembly notch in the bottom of the slide.
steps.cite: Kimber CDS9 Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Reassembly

steps.title: Slide stop out from the right, slide forward
steps.action: Holding that position, push in on the protruding end of the slide stop pin on the RIGHT side with a finger or a tool and take the stop out from the left. Then run the slide assembly forward off the frame.
steps.quote: Slide the slide assembly forward and off the frame.
steps.cite: Kimber CDS9 Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Reassembly

steps.title: ⛔ Slide is off — do NOT touch the thumb safety
steps.action: This is the CDS9's own trap. With the slide removed, do not push the thumb safety to ON: the detent plunger underneath is under spring tension with nothing retaining it, and it can leave the frame hard enough to injure. Eye protection stays on.
steps.quote: Once the slide is removed DO NOT engage the thumb safety into the “ON” position. Doing so could cause the thumb safety detent plunger to spring out from the frame.
steps.cite: Kimber CDS9 Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Reassembly

steps.title: Guide and springs out, then the barrel over its cam
steps.action: Lift the recoil spring guide and spring slightly, then withdraw the assembly toward the rear of the slide, and take the OUTER spring off the guide rod without bending it. Then lift the barrel and move it rearward out of the slide — it rides a cam, not a link. Strip complete.
steps.aside: Remove the barrel from the slide by first lifting, then moving the barrel to the rear out away from the slide.
steps.quote: Remove the outer recoil spring from the guide rod while being careful not to bend the spring.
steps.cite: Kimber CDS9 Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Reassembly

steps.title: ⛔ Rod in from the CHAMBER end, every time
steps.action: The cleaning rod enters at the chamber, never the muzzle. Wet patch with bore solvent, let it soak a few minutes, dry patch to lift the loose debris — and read the solvent maker's own directions, because some of them will lift a finish as happily as they lift fouling.
steps.aside: Run a patch wet with bore cleaning solvent through the barrel and let the solution soak
steps.quote: Always insert a cleaning rod from the chamber end of the barrel.
steps.cite: Kimber CDS9 Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING

steps.title: Wet brush through and OUT the muzzle, then repeat to clean
steps.action: Push the wet bore brush in at the chamber and all the way OUT of the muzzle before drawing it back — reversing a brush inside the bore folds the bristles over. Dry patch after, and repeat the pair until a patch comes out clean. Then a light oil, and ⛔ a dry patch through before you ever fire it.
steps.aside: Run a dry patch through the barrel before firing to remove oil.
steps.quote: Run a wet bore brush through the chamber end of the barrel and out the muzzle, making several passes.
steps.cite: Kimber CDS9 Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING

steps.title: Breech face and every bearing surface — nylon brush
steps.action: Wipe the dirt off all the bearing surfaces on the slide and frame, then get into the breech face and the rest of the parts with a toothbrush or similar nylon brush. ⛔ And no ultrasonic tank: Kimber says damage from one is not covered by warranty, and night sights must never go near it.
steps.aside: Do not expose night sights to an ultrasonic cleaning environment.
steps.quote: Clean the breech face and all parts (a toothbrush or similar nylon brush works well).
steps.cite: Kimber CDS9 Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING

steps.title: Lubricate by the drop, at the points Kimber names
steps.action: Premium oil, not grease — and if it carries Teflon, shake it, because the Teflon settles overnight and you will otherwise apply the carrier and none of the additive. Then oil only where this book says, in the quantities it gives.
steps.aside: Barrel cam; 1 drop inside barrel cam.
steps.quote: Slide and frame rails; 3 drops on each side.
steps.cite: Kimber CDS9 Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — LUBRICATION

steps.title: ⛔ Nothing in the firing pin channel, and wipe the excess
steps.action: Reassemble, work the slide five or six times, dry fire, then wipe off the excess. Moderation is the whole point: too little and it wears, too much and it collects the grit that wears it faster. ⛔ And if it has been stored oiled, a dry patch goes through the barrel before firing.
steps.quote: If the firearm has been stored with oil in the barrel and chamber, push a dry patch through the barrel before firing.
steps.cite: Kimber CDS9 Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — LUBRICATION

deepAbsentReason: Kimber's limit is printed in the strip itself — "The firearm is now disassembled. No further disassembly is required for general cleaning." — and again as a warning: "Do not disassemble your firearm beyond field stripping outlined in this manual. Do not manipulate any internal components beyond what you are instructed to do in this manual." Going further voids the warranty in Kimber's own words. A manufacturer's published DON'T outranks every other tier, so nothing deeper is authored from anywhere else.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: ⛔ Rod ALWAYS from the chamber end
Wet patch, soak a few minutes, dry patch
Wet brush in at the chamber and OUT the muzzle before drawing back
Repeat until a patch comes out clean, then a light oil

cleaning.name: SLIDE & FRAME
tasks: Breech face and parts with a nylon brush
⛔ No ultrasonic cleaning — the damage is not warranted

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Premium oil, NOT grease; shake it if it contains Teflon
Only the points this model's book names, in the drops it gives
⛔ Never into the firing pin channel
Work the slide 5-6 times, dry fire, wipe the excess off

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Wiped clean; follower checked to slide freely

reassembly: Barrel into the slide, entered from above and moved forward onto its cam.
⛔ Recoil spring slid down the guide rod until SEATED against the base of the rod; outer spring back on without bending it.
Guide and spring assembly into the slide from the rear.
Slide onto the frame, run back until the slide stop tab meets the disassembly notch.
Slide stop in from the left, pushed home from the right; cycle, dry fire, wipe off excess.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded: the recoil spring must be slid all the way down the guide rod until it is SEATED against the base — Kimber prints that instruction twice. Then work the slide five or six times, confirm it returns to battery, dry fire and wipe the excess off. Check the thumb safety operates now that the slide is back on.
